notes: Google's Gemini 4 Argon launch evidence, retrieved 2026-10-13. HEADLINE TABLE: 19 benchmark rows x 4 columns (Gemini 4 Argon, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5), 76 cells of which 3 are dashes (Agent's Last Exam Fable 5.1; OSWorld-2.0 Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5), so 73 cells are stored. The table is an IMAGE (blog 2026-09-30 original_images/gemini-4-argon_table_blog.gif, 3936x3948; the same image on page 5 of the methodology PDF and printed page 5 (PDF page 6) of the model card); no HTML table exists. Read visually at full resolution, then checked with tesseract OCR twice (whole image, which skips the blue Argon cells, and a thresholded Argon column): every OCR token agreed with the visual read apart from decimal-point slips (74.1 read as 741, 77.9 as 779), and the Argon column was cross-checked against the six single-benchmark bar charts on the 2026-09-30 post (Vals Index, AutomationBench, Vals Finance Agent v2, Harvey, DeepSWE, plus the CWE-bench leaderboard chart), all of which print the same values. Values are stored as fractions (68.9% -> 0.689). Shading in the image (blue = Argon best, grey = another model best) agrees with the numeric order on every row. EFFORT: Google's methodology says Argon runs use 'the highest thinking settings' (the API offers low, medium, high), so Google-computed Argon rows (DeepSWE, Terminal-bench 4.0, PostTrainBench, Terminal-Bench Science, LABBench 2, GraphWalks, Agent's Last Exam, OSWorld-2.0, LVBench) carry effort high with that wording in effort_verbatim. Argon rows sourced from third-party leaderboards carry unknown. Competitor columns carry unknown with the methodology's wording ('maximum thinking/reasoning settings available ... best available reasoning results when reported results are not available'). No row carries an effort Google did not state. PROVENANCE and caveats: per-row sourcing notes are quoted verbatim in each row's caveat. Google self-computed Argon on DeepSWE, Terminal-bench 4.0, Terminal-Bench Science, LABBench 2, GraphWalks, PostTrainBench (all models), Agent's Last Exam, OSWorld-2.0 and LVBench; competitor values on those rows come from leaderboards, system cards, blog posts or Google's own runs as the methodology states. Vendor-published, comparable false, grade C, a separate comparability_group per metric, kept apart from third-party board readings of the same models (for example the Vals, AA and tbench.ai Argon rows in the 2026-10-07 and lane-B files). BLOG-ONLY CHARTS (2026-09-30 post images with printed value labels): CWE-bench v1 leaderboard (9 stored of 11 bars), Gray Swan IPI attack success at k=15 (12 stored of 13 bars), Real-world Vulnerability Discovery and Wiz Penetration Test Benchmark (Argon vs Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber; only Argon stored). Bars whose model has no registry id (Hy4 Preview, Inkling on CWE-bench; Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber on Gray Swan, vulnerability discovery and the Wiz benchmark) are named in the caveats or missing, not stored. The Gray Swan chart's k=1 and k=10 segments and the CWE-bench Pass@4 tiebreak values have no printed labels and are not digitized. The 2026-09-30 post's bar charts for Vals Index, AutomationBench, Vals Finance Agent v2, Harvey and DeepSWE repeat table values and are not stored twice. CONFLICTS and cross-source observations (stored side by side, not reconciled): (1) Google's Vals Index cell 68.9 equals the Vals board's 68.90 for Argon on 2026-10-07 but Opus 5.5 is 67.0 here versus 66.97 on that board and Sonnet 5.5 is not in Google's table; (2) Google's Terminal-bench 4.0 cell for Argon (57.4, self-computed) differs from the 57.58 Vals Terminal-Bench 4.0 reading recorded on 2026-10-07; (3) the Meta Muse Wonder launch table lists DeepSWE 1.1 Opus 5.5 74.2, GPT-6 Astra 74.1 and Fable 5.1 67.4, the same numbers as Google's columns, so Google and Meta both quote the same upstream leaderboard or system-card values; (4) Artificial Analysis's own DeepSWE v1.1 coding-agents run (artificial-analysis-coding-agents-muse-wonder-2026-10-13.json, Antigravity CLI, effort high) has Argon at 78.8% against Google's 77.9%, and puts Opus 5.5 at 68.4% (Google 74.2%), GPT-6 Astra at 67.6% (Google 74.1%) and Fable 5.1 at 64.3% (Google 67.4%), so the competitor gap in Google's table is larger than on AA's run. Recheck the third-party boards by 2026-10-20 (lane-B coverage file).

claims.statement: Google's launch table (Gemini 4 Argon model card printed page 5, methodology PDF page 5, 2026-09-30 post) compares Gemini 4 Argon with GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5 on 19 benchmark rows. Argon has the highest cell on 14 rows (Vals Index, AutomationBench, Vals Finance Agent v2, Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark, DeepSWE v1.1, Vibe Code Bench, LABBench 2, RiemannBench, GraphWalks up to 128k, GraphWalks 256k to 1M, Agent's Last Exam, Chartography, LVBench, and CWE-bench v1 as a tie with GPT-6 Astra at 68.0%). It is not the highest on FrontierSWE v2 (GPT-6 Astra 65.5% vs Argon 55.0%), Terminal-bench 4.0 (Opus 5.5 66.4% vs 57.4%), PostTrainBench (Opus 5.5 49.3% vs 45.3%), Terminal-Bench Science 0.1 (GPT-6 Astra 68.1% vs 57.6%) and OSWorld-2.0 offline partial (GPT-6 Astra 72.6% vs 69.2%).
claims.implication: Vendor table with mixed provenance per row (Google self-computed runs for Argon on about half the rows, third-party leaderboards on the rest, system-card or leaderboard numbers for competitors, different harnesses and frame budgets). No intervals, run counts or per-effort values. Treat as leads, not a ranking. Largest Argon deficits are on terminal and SWE agent harness benchmarks (FrontierSWE, Terminal-bench 4.0, Terminal-Bench Science).

claims.statement: Google's methodology page says 'All of the results are run with the Gemini API with the highest thinking settings unless indicated otherwise below' and for GPT-6 Astra, Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 'we default to reporting maximum thinking/reasoning settings available, but when reported results are not available we use best available reasoning results.' Argon's API default thinking level is medium; Google publishes no low or medium scores.
claims.implication: Published Argon numbers are high-effort (the top documented level) and the competitor columns are best-effort max or best available, not matched efforts. Medium (the default) and low have no first-party quality evidence.

claims.statement: Vendor safety claims (not verified): Gray Swan IPI attack success across 15 adaptive attempts 0.7% (lowest on Google's chart; Claude Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 1.0%); shortcut or cheating attempts on coding benchmarks 'dropped to just 2%'; external bio red teaming 'could only unlock less than 1% of bio sub-tasks'; violations on an adversarial set 'reduced nearly 2-fold'; solved all 12 end-to-end simulated cyberattack scenarios (up from five).
claims.implication: All of this is Google-authored; mitigations (input screening, activation probes, continuous monitoring) apply to the production deployment. The unmitigated cyber capability is the reason Google keeps a separate allowlisted Cyber Permissive variant.

claims.statement: Google states Argon is 'ranking #1 on the Vals Index' and launched at an introductory $2 / $10 per 1M tokens (cached input 95% off), rising to $4 / $20 after November 30, 2026. At the Google table's own cell values Argon's Vals Index lead over Claude Opus 5.5 is 1.9 points (68.9% vs 67.0%) and over Fable 5.1 3.1 points; no interval is published.
claims.implication: A lead of under two points on one index at intro pricing says nothing about standard-price cost per success; at $4 / $20 the output price doubles.

claims.statement: Launch-post prose figures with no comparison table: ERQA 87% ('outperforms all other frontier models'); Gamow Labs private evals RareBench 57% (rare-disease diagnosis assistance) and LabBench 52.2% (wet-lab reasoning) described as topping those evals; Argon in Antigravity 'increase[d] agentic code submissions by more than 35% while reducing code rollbacks by nearly a third' inside Google. Gamow Labs evals are private and the blog footnote says external views are not Google's.
claims.implication: Anecdotal or private; do not use for routing.
